title: Exploring Mode Connectivity in Krylov Subspace for Domain Generalization
claim: Optimization can be framed as a billiard ball: line search finds loss-contour boundaries, then reflection redirects the trajectory to stay in low-loss regions.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, physical analogy then line-search plot then reflection geometry
description: Three labeled panels. (a) Billiard Game: a green pool table with a brown rim and black pockets. A white ball sits on the table and a ghosted trail with a red arrow shows it bouncing off a cushion. (b) Line Search: a convex loss curve over a horizontal parameter axis, cut by a dashed black threshold line labeled l_th. Red and blue dashed vertical markers show probe points x1, x2, x3 at step sizes h, 2h, 4h (red, small h) and h, h/2, h/4 (blue, large h). Arrows under and over the curve mark the step lengths, and a legend names the two colors. (c) Reflection: a black kidney-shaped loss contour with points θ0, θ1, θ2. A red arrow p0 runs from θ0 to the boundary point θ1. A green arrow p1 leaves θ1 toward θ2. A dashed normal n1 and equal angles φ show the reflection, with the update formula written beside the green arrow. The eye goes first to the green table, then to the colorful line-search plot.
caption: Overview of the proposed Billiard Optimization Algorithm (BOA). (a) A schematic diagram of a billiards game on a two-dimensional table; (b) The first operation of BOA (Line Search): Like a ball approaching a cushion, this operation identifies loss contour boundaries through line search along directional vectors. (c) The second operation of BOA (Reflection): Upon boundary contact, the trajectory redirects via physics-based rules, mimicking a ball’s reflection off a cushion.
abstract: This paper explores the geometric characteristics of loss landscapes to enhance domain generalization (DG) in deep neural networks. Existing methods mainly leverage the local flatness around minima for improved generalization. However, recent theoretical studies indicate that flatness does not universally guarantee better generalization. Instead, this paper investigates a global geometrical property for domain generalization, i.e., \emph{mode connectivity}, the phenomenon where distinct local minima are connected by continuous low-loss pathways. Different from flatness, mode connectivity enables transitions from poor to superior generalization models without leaving low-loss regions. To navigate these connected pathways effectively, this paper proposes a novel Billiard Optimization Algorithm (BOA), which discovers superior models by mimicking billiard dynamics. During this process, BOA operates within a low-dimensional Krylov subspace, aiming to alleviate the curse of dimensionality caused by the high-dimensional parameter space of deep models. Furthermore, this paper reveals that oracle test gradients strongly align with the Krylov subspace constructed from training gradients across diverse datasets and architectures. This alignment offers a powerful tool to bridge training and test domains, enabling the efficient discovery of superior models with limited training domains. Experiments on DomainBed demonstrate that BOA consistently outperforms existing sharpness-aware and DG methods across diverse datasets and architectures. Impressively, BOA even surpasses the sharpness-aware minimization by 3.6\% on VLCS when using a ViT-B/16 backbone.
